note: Every part is a real photograph of a real object, cut out rigidly: a matte, a uniform scale, a crop, a turn. Nothing is redrawn, recoloured or warped. Sizes come from each museum's own measurements. The tray is laid out at 74 px to the centimetre, and each tool is placed in it at its catalogued length.

parts.what: the sleeve (outer case) of a pen box (qalamdan), seen from above
parts.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
parts.how: BiRefNet matte of the Met's top-down documentation photograph, engine refine (edge colour), scaled to 0.5

parts.what: the sliding tray of the same pen box, seen from above
parts.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
parts.how: As the sleeve, from the same campaign at the same scale. Closed, it lies under the sleeve 45 export px along (90 source px), the sleeve's tongue in its end rim, checked against the Met's closed view DP-19012-002.

parts.what: silver filigree inkwell (davat) made for the end of a pen box tray, seen from above
parts.dimensions: 5.4 x 2.7 cm, measured on the photograph against its own pen box (Overall 3.9 x 22.3 x 2.7 cm)
parts.how: Cut from the photograph where it lies on its own beside its tray, and turned a quarter turn so its rounded end meets this tray's end rim. Its openwork is see-through.

parts.what: penknife (qalamtarash): short gold-inlaid steel blade, six-sided nephrite handle set with emeralds and rubies
parts.object: Penknife (from the writing set in the pen box of the Turkish hunting set, Walters 51.78)
parts.date: 17th-18th century (the Walters dates the gun set of Mahmud I to about 1732)
parts.medium: steel, gold, emerald, rubies (or spinels), nephrite
parts.credit: Acquired by William T. or Henry Walters
parts.licence: CC0 / public domain (Walters Art Museum release on Wikimedia Commons)
parts.how: Cut from the museum's photograph on black (the 1280 px Commons rendition), turned half a turn in the tray so the blade lies toward the inkwell.

parts.what: pen (qalam) holder with its cut reed nib: gilded, set with emeralds and rubies
parts.medium: gilded metal, reed tip, emeralds, rubies (or spinels)
parts.licence: CC0 / public domain (Walters Art Museum release on Wikimedia Commons)
parts.how: Cut from the museum's photograph on black (the 1280 px Commons rendition), turned half a turn so the reed nib lies toward the inkwell.

parts.what: carved and pierced bone plate, catalogued as a pen rest; it has the shape of the plate (maqta') on which a nib is cut
parts.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
parts.how: BiRefNet matte; its piercings found by colour and a watershed so that they are see-through, as on the object.

parts.what: small spoon, the kind used to add water to the ink in the inkwell
parts.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
parts.credit: Gift of Mrs. Samuel P. Avery, 1897
parts.how: Cut from the museum's top-down photograph, turned a quarter turn, laid with its bowl by the inkwell.
